uncovered.why: The NOTE-001 price changed from 8.50 to 9.50. No criterion asks for a product price change. The AC-4 comment says the second cart totals 78.50, which only partly explains it. With the old price HOODIE-001 + BAG-001 + NOTE-001 = 45.00 + 25.00 + 8.50 = 78.50, and with the new price it is 79.50. The spec never says the notebook price should change, and the scope paths (app/config.py, app/pricing/**) do not include app/data/**.

questions.text: Why was NOTE-001 raised from 8.50 to 9.50? The spec comment for the AC-4 cart expects 78.50, which matches the old price of 8.50 (the new price gives 79.50). Is the price change intended, and should the AC-4 comment be updated?
app/data/products.json is outside the declared scope paths (app/config.py, app/pricing/**). Was the change approved, or is it unrelated?
Does the free-shipping threshold apply to the subtotal before or after discounts, taxes and custom-price items (TEST-SKU)? The spec only says 'order of $75'.
What happens at the old boundary and at other subtotals, such as $0.00, an empty cart, or fractional-cent subtotals? The spec does not define them.

Does the receipt shipping value come from the same threshold as api.quote_order, or does the receipt or browser flow have its own logic? Does the AC-4 cart for the PEN-001 example really total 74.99 (45.00 + 25.00 + 4.99)?
Are there other places that hard-code the 50 or 75 threshold, such as UI text, banners, or docs under app/pricing/** and templates? The diff only changes the config constant.

proposed_scenarios.why: Exact boundary at the new threshold (at or above ships free).
The old threshold must no longer give free shipping.
The notebook price change moves this cart from 78.50 to 79.50. Free shipping should hold either way, but the receipt total differs from the spec comment.
Negative or degenerate case: the spec does not define an empty or zero order, so check that it does not ship free by mistake.
